meta.name: NeuroSage exercise catalog
meta.status: DRAFT — not clinically validated; requires domain-expert sign-off before use (per proposal IT23242722, Objective I).
design_rules: The cognitive TARGET is fixed per exercise and never changed by theme or difficulty.
DIFFICULTY is controlled separately by the adaptive staircase (see difficulty_axes); it is NOT encoded here as fixed levels.
THEME/CONTENT is a personalization wrapper applied AFTER an exercise is selected; it changes context only, not the task.
Exercises are drawn from established programs/paradigms — none are invented.
Effect sizes are population averages (Hill et al. 2017) with wide CIs; treat as a trainability prior, not a per-patient guarantee.

exercises.name: Spaced retrieval
exercises.task: Recall target information (e.g., a name–object pair, a fact) over gradually expanding time intervals.

exercises.name: Errorless learning
exercises.task: Learn/relearn target information while errors during encoding are prevented (cues given before any guess).
exercises.benefit_note: supports encoding in AD; evidence mixed in MCI

exercises.name: Sequence / list recall
exercises.task: Recall a sequence of items or everyday events in order after a delay.
exercises.benefit_note: verbal memory g=0.42; working memory g=0.74 when span-based

exercises.name: Speed-of-processing / Useful Field of View
exercises.task: Rapidly identify and locate briefly shown targets across the visual field; speeded responses.

exercises.name: Cancellation / visual search
exercises.task: Find and mark all target items among distractors; sustained and selective attention.

exercises.name: Digit span / divided attention
exercises.task: Hold and reproduce sequences; or respond to two streams at once (divided attention).
exercises.benefit_note: attention g=0.44; overlaps working memory g=0.74

exercises.name: n-back / working-memory updating
exercises.task: Indicate when the current stimulus matches the one n steps earlier; continuous updating.

exercises.name: Task-switching / set-shifting
exercises.task: Alternate between two rules/categories on cue; measures cognitive flexibility.

exercises.name: Planning / inhibition
exercises.task: Plan a multi-step solution (Tower-type) or suppress a prepotent response (Stroop-type).

exercises.name: Verbal fluency
exercises.task: Generate as many words as possible in a category or starting letter within a time limit.
exercises.benefit_note: language g=0.41 but wide CI (uncertain — flag)
exercises.localization_note: High language dependency — requires Sinhala/Tamil adaptation (ITC guidelines) before counting as validated in-language.

exercises.name: Confrontation naming / word-finding
exercises.task: Name depicted objects/actions; retrieve the correct word under cueing if needed.
exercises.localization_note: Images and target words must be culturally/linguistically familiar in Sinhala/Tamil.

exercises.name: Semantic categorization / association
exercises.task: Sort words/pictures into categories or match related concepts.

exercises.name: Figure copying / construction
exercises.task: Reproduce or assemble a geometric figure/arrangement from a model.

exercises.name: Mental rotation / spatial reasoning
exercises.task: Decide whether rotated shapes match; reason about spatial relations.

exercises.name: Visual search / spatial puzzle
exercises.task: Locate targets by spatial layout, or complete a jigsaw/matching puzzle.

personalization.principle: Relevance-first. Personal history and interests carry the reminiscence/person-centred benefit; age is a secondary proxy. Theme changes CONTENT only — never the cognitive target or the difficulty.

age_bands.label: Young / early-onset (< 65)
age_bands.basis: Young-onset dementia = onset before 65 (convention based on retirement age, not biology).
age_bands.content_framing: Working-age life: work schedules, family logistics, finances, active roles. Avoid retirement/household-only content (can feel irrelevant/infantilising).

age_bands.label: Late-onset (>= 65)
age_bands.basis: Typical dementia population; remote autobiographical memory relatively preserved.
age_bands.content_framing: Household routines, appointments, remote life history / reminiscence themes.

relevance_factors.personal_history: occupation, hometown, family, notable life events (user/carer supplied)

theme_examples.note: EXAMPLES ONLY — confirm with supervisor/clinician; not validated themes.

attention_search.late_onset: find items in a familiar kitchen scene
attention_search.interest:gardening: find specific plants/tools in a garden scene

personalization.gender_policy: Do not auto-assign themes by gender. Record only if a justified research reason exists. Drive themes from stated interests (person-centred).

presentation_profiles.note: Accessibility layer; independent of cognitive target and difficulty. User override always available.

default_older.palette: high-contrast; avoid blue/green distinctions; prefer red/orange/yellow

cross_cutting.cognitive_stimulation_therapy: CST / reminiscence (reality orientation, themed quiz, autobiographical content) — broad engagement layer, NICE-recommended for mild-moderate dementia. Feeds the engagement criterion; not a single-domain exercise.

governance.validation_status: Draft catalog. Exercises are evidence-based paradigms; the domain/arm/theme tagging is NOT yet clinically validated.
governance.required_signoff: Domain expert / clinician must confirm tagging is clinically appropriate before deployment (proposal Objective I & II).
honest_flags: LBD-priority domains (visuospatial 0.18, executive 0.20, processing speed 0.09) are the WEAKEST CCT responders — keep as targets but set low expected benefit; lean on working memory (0.74) and attention (0.44) and compensatory strategies.
Memory strategy training shows mixed/negative results in MCI; prefer errorless learning / spaced retrieval (compensatory) for the AD arm.
High-language exercises (fluency, naming, semantic) need proper Sinhala/Tamil adaptation before counting as validated in-language.
